ai.name: DeepSeek
ai.hook: DeepSeek ships V4-Flash open weights, nearly matching GPT-5.6 Luna at 60% lower cost.
insights: **Terminal-Bench score of 82.7**, close to **GPT-5.6 Luna's 51** despite no architecture change, just better post-training
**284B total / 13B active params**, **1M context**, MIT license, quantized to **4-bit and 3-bit** for local runs
**98% cache-hit discount** makes repeated agentic calls extremely cheap
ai.for_you: A model this cheap with 1M context and MIT licensing is worth testing as the backend for a PT SMB chatbot pilot, since your client margins depend entirely on inference cost per task, not just quality.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: concrete, MIT-licensed, immediately usable release beating a stale week of 'not much happened' news

ai.name: Interconnects
ai.hook: Open-weight models are in a genuine six-month survival test against closed labs.
insights: **Kimi K3** (2.8T params, 104B active) and **GLM-5.2** mark a real capability step-change for open agents
The open-closed performance gap is narrowing fast, per UK AISI's own cyber capability analysis
Running frontier open models now needs **8x MI355X GPUs minimum**, pricing out most indie builders from self-hosting
ai.for_you: The gap closing means your agency's pitch can lean on cheaper open models via hosted APIs (Together, Baseten) instead of OpenAI, but self-hosting Kimi-class models is not realistic for PT SMB budgets, stick to hosted access.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: most substantive analysis of the open-vs-closed dynamic shaping which models Pedro should actually build on

ai.name: Simon Willison
ai.hook: 235 AI companies including OpenAI sign an open letter on open weights and US AI leadership.
insights: Letter shepherded by **Microsoft**, dated July 24th, signed by NVIDIA, Amazon, YC, Linux Foundation, and later OpenAI
Frames open weights as a national competitiveness issue, not just a developer preference
Comes the same month OpenAI open-sourced its Codex Security CLI, reinforcing the open-tooling push
ai.for_you: No direct action here, filed for awareness, but it signals more free, high-quality open tooling is coming that your agency can build on without vendor lock-in.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: signals policy direction that affects which models/tools remain freely usable for a bootstrapped agency

ai.name: OpenAI
ai.hook: OpenAI uses an internal AI system to produce ten new results in math and theoretical CS.
insights: Follows Anthropic's earlier use of Claude (Mythos Preview) to find real cryptographic weaknesses, spending $100k in tokens
OpenAI set an internal model loose on genuinely hard open problems, not benchmark tasks
Part of a pattern: frontier labs proving research-grade reasoning, not just chat quality
ai.for_you: No direct action here, filed for awareness, this is lab-scale research work far outside SMB agency use cases.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: notable capability proof point, distinct from the routine price-cut and benchmark news dominating this week

ai.name: Import AI
ai.hook: AI agents can now complete week-long programming tasks, but still fail the hardest ones.
insights: **Epoch and METR** release **MirrorCode**, a benchmark for long-horizon programming task completion
Systems succeed on multi-day tasks but still can't crack the hardest problems, described as 'good' for safety
Separately, UK AISI finds the open-vs-closed model gap on cyber capability is shrinking fast
ai.for_you: Long-horizon task completion is directly relevant to how much you can delegate to an agent when building the micro-SaaS, worth testing a multi-day agent run on a real feature instead of one-shot prompts.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: concrete new benchmark result, more substantive than repeated 'not much happened' recaps

ai.name: Latent Space (Ontologies post)
ai.hook: AI engineers are reviving ontologies to keep unpredictable agents inside deterministic rails.
insights: Semantic web concepts, once dismissed, are back as guardrails for agentic systems
Ontologies define what an agent is allowed to reason about and how, reducing hallucination scope
Framed as a practical fix, not a research curiosity
ai.for_you: Worth stealing for the agency: define a small ontology (services, prices, booking rules) for each SMB client's chatbot so the agent can't invent policies or prices that don't exist.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: directly actionable technique for reliability, rare in a week dominated by model releases

build_this.name: DeepSeek-V4-Flash API (open weights)
build_this.what_it_is: An open, MIT-licensed model matching near-frontier benchmark scores at a fraction of the cost, quantizable to 4-bit.
build_this.why_try_it: Swap it into your current agency chatbot stack for one client this week and compare cost-per-conversation against whatever you're using now, the 98% cache-hit discount could meaningfully change your margin on repeat-query bots.

build_this.name: Ontology-constrained agent design
build_this.what_it_is: A technique for scoping what an AI agent can talk about and how, using a lightweight domain ontology instead of open-ended prompting.
build_this.why_try_it: Build a simple ontology (services, hours, prices, FAQs) for one existing SMB client and rewire their chatbot to only reason within it, this is a concrete fix for the 'agent invents a price' problem you've likely already hit.

tech.for_you: If Google Overviews keep cannibalizing organic traffic, SEO-driven lead gen for your SMB clients becomes less reliable, worth pricing in paid or WhatsApp-first acquisition channels for pitches.
